trusted_contracts: Torch randn/zeros return fresh contiguous fp16 tensors of requested shape on CUDA when their primitive call succeeds.
randn samples are arbitrary fp16 words; no probability distribution is used.
Torch allocation failure, Python shape conversion and unsupported caller types are ordinary allocation-call primitive failures (the observed boolean second argument reaches zeros before rejection).
Triton JIT/driver and backend/runtime errors propagate from the single launch call. Successful execution is proved by the actual interpreter; there is no arbitrary final-value result.
limitations: CUDA requests redirected to meta device for metadata evidence.
Injected errors test source call wiring only; they do not prove allocator/runtime implementation or all Python caller classifications.
No GPU or full native backend execution.
